note: A small stretch of a Byzantine role-play city, after the RP cities of The Specialists: shops below and homes above along a colonnaded street, one square with a column. The building rules are the house's where they apply (checkStyle reads them by name); `site` holds the rules of the street, the porticoes, the square and the properties, which a site check measures. Sizes of rooms come from architecture.json as the house's do; sizes of streets and squares are the measured bands of the three RP cities (levels/notes-rp-city.md), in cells of 64 (1.6256 m). A rule is added only with a source or a fault found in the game.

sources.neufert: E. and P. Neufert, Architects' Data; scaled to the games in architecture.json (scale)
sources.alexander: C. Alexander et al., A Pattern Language (OUP 1977); patterns by number
sources.rp-cities: the three RP cities H9 plays (Alexandria, Paradise City, Xenon City), measured as levels/notes-rp-city.md says: bands are their median and extremes
sources.h9-redesign: the person's complaints about New Byzantium (levels/notes-h9.md, section 5, from REDESIGN.md) and what the RP game needs of a map (section 2)
sources.mese: the Mese of Constantinople: the city's main street, lined on both sides by colonnaded porticoes with shops under them, opening into the Forum of Constantine, round, with his porphyry column in the middle
sources.walk-2026-11-02: the person's walk of smak_house01 in Half-Life on 2026-11-02: a one-edge door could not be passed with its leaf open
sources.pieces-2026-11-03: the Mese pieces' pictures, approved on 2026-11-03: a portico one cell deep leaves about 36 units between a column's base and the wall, the player's width

area.says: a room's cells are within its kind's area (minArea to maxArea of architecture.json, in cells)

minSide.says: the largest rectangle inside a room is at least its kind's minSide across, in cells (and 2, the depth a door's leaf swings into)

compact.says: the largest rectangle inside a room holds at least this share of its cells (not halls and landings)

window.says: a room of these kinds has a window on an outside wall (patterns 159, 180); a shop's is its shop window on the street

frontWindow.says: a room of these kinds has a window on the front wall: a shop's shop window on the street, beside its door (pattern 165, opening to the street)

front.says: every entrance (the shop's own door, the stair hall's) stands on the front wall, the street's side (pattern 165, opening to the street; the Mese's shops stood under its porticoes); and a kitchen deeper from the front than a living room, as the house's

gradient.says: every room is reached from its entrance without passing through a private room, but the pairs listed

property.says: every shop and every home is one property: its own door from public floor (the street, the portico, a stair hall), named, opened by use; no property is reached through another's door (the RP plugin hands the name out as a key)

homesShare.says: homes are at least this share of the properties (the person: more homes than stores; New Byzantium's districts were shop-heavy)

shopOnStreet.says: a shop's own door and window stand on the street side, under the portico (pattern 165, opening to the street; the Mese's shops stood under its porticoes)

porticoDepth.says: a portico is at least this many cells deep from the column line to the shop fronts

streetWidth.says: the street's open carriageway, between the porticoes' column lines, is within the RP cities' street under sky (7.4 to 15.2 m, median 10.2 m)

square.says: the square is 12 m across or more both ways, 150 m2 or more, its box no longer than 3 to 1 (the cities' plaza; their median plaza is 229 m2), with the column in its middle and 2 cells clear round the column's steps

uniqueFootprints.says: no two buildings share a footprint, and at most this share of rooms share a shape (stair halls and landings left out: the one stair piece makes them alike; the cities repeat no building and 5 to 20 % of rooms; New Byzantium repeated 76 % of buildings and was called carbon copies)

roomsBrighter.says: rooms are lit brighter than the street at the median (the cities: rooms 68 to 71 of 255 against streets 53 to 56; New Byzantium did the opposite)

spawns.says: player starts stand on public floor, clear of every door's swing, at least this far apart (TS reads the first 32)
